messages:
lina_support: FYI a couple of paying customers filed p99 latency complaints starting ~01:20 UTC after last runtime deploy. They attached traces that show attention kernel falling back to SDPA for long seqs. Can eng-runtime take a look? :rotating_light:
marc_engineer: pinging here. do we have model + seq len from the traces?
lina_support: customer A = redwood/gpt-neo-3b@v2, seq=2048->response spikes to 3.2s p99 (was ~800ms). traces show lines like: `kernel_select: candidate=flash_attn_v2, fallback=sdpa, reason=heuristic_mismatch` and `compile_flags: -O3 -mavx2 -DENABLE_FLASH_ATTENTION=1`
marc_engineer: hmm, heuristic_mismatch means the kernel-cost estimator picked SDPA. did the cost model change in the deploy? I saw a small kernel-priority tweak earlier.
nate_oncall: @marc_engineer I rolled the runtime patch at 01:15 UTC that updated compile heuristics and the sdpa priority table. Could be correlated. Oncall notes show transient cpu/gpu steal in one shard, but not widespread.
sara_sre: marking incident-hot. can we reproduce quickly with a minimal request? If yes we can confirm whether fallback is deterministic.
marc_engineer: repro steps I used locally:
```
# reproduce script
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'X-Model: redwood/gpt-neo-3b@v2' \
  -d '{"input":"a"*1500, "max_tokens":512, "temperature":0.0}'
```
It toggles between flash_attn_v2 and sdpa depending on batch/seq mix. Logs: `kernel=flash_attn_v2 pid=... time=120ms` then next request `kernel=sdpa pid=... time=980ms`
olivia_pm: customer impact? any billing or data loss?
lina_support: no errors, just high tails. customers are warning about latency for interactive use. Asking for ETA on mitigation.
marc_engineer: immediate mitigation options: 1) force flash_attn on for the model (config rollout) 2) roll back the heuristic change 3) temporary model variant pin to a known-good kernel. Forcing flash_attn may increase OOM risk on extreme batches.
nate_oncall: we can push a conservative rollout: on one zone enable `flash_pref=high` for canary fleet. command: `kerneltuner set-pref --model redwood/gpt-neo-3b@v2 --pref flash=prefer --scope canary-us-west`
sara_sre: can we do that and monitor p95/p99 in the console? set 30m canary and auto rollback on p99>1s.
marc_engineer: agreed. also need to check compile flags: the new change introduced `-DENABLE_FLASH_ATTENTION=1` but we added an optimization that makes the cost-estimator penalize flash when sequence distribution is bimodal. that penalty may be too large. I'll open a PR to adjust the penalty constant and run perf harness.
marc_engineer: quick log excerpt (from canary node):
```
[01:22:10] kernel_select: model=gpt-neo-3b seq=1900 cost_flash=48.7 cost_sdpa=46.2 -> pick=sdpa
[01:22:11] kernel_exec: sdpa tokens=512 latency=940ms
[01:22:12] kv_cache: hit=0 prefix_len=512
```
lina_support: customer A says toggling a "compatibility" flag on their end temporarily helped because it lowered sent batch sizes. Not great but gives clue it's a batching/heuristic interplay.
marc_engineer: actionable plan: (A) start canary rollout forcing flash preference in us-west (nate) (B) revert kernel-priority delta in a staging branch (me) (C) run perf harness across seq distribution to tune estimator (me + eng-ml) (D) notify customers with ETA (~2 hours) (sara/lina)
nate_oncall: starting canary now: `kerneltuner set-pref --model redwood/gpt-neo-3b@v2 --pref flash=prefer --scope canary-us-west --duration 30m` (executed) :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: canary config applied to 12 pods in us-west, change id=cfg-2026-4444, monitoring hook enabled.
olivia_pm: thanks. please keep me posted on customer comms.
marc_engineer: meanwhile I'll run a quick binary search on the penalty constant. if we can prove estimator is misranking flash for 1600-2200 seqs we'll push a hotfix.
sara_sre: also think about a graceful degradation: if flash fails with OOM, fallback to sdpa but cap batch size so latency doesn't jump 3x. add to runbook.
lina_support: customer-facing message drafted: "We're investigating unusual tail latency, temporary mitigation applied, working on a permanent fix; next update in 2h." sending now. :thumbsup:
marc_engineer: leaving trace flags in canary to capture cost metrics: `RUNTIME_TRACE_KERNEL_COST=1`
nate_oncall: canary p99 after 5m: baseline ~750ms -> now 820ms, p95 stable. looks promising. keep monitoring.
olivia_pm: if canary holds we'll schedule a controlled global rollout.
sara_sre: open follow-up tickets: #perf-estimator-tune, #kernel-priority-revert, #customer-comms-4444440000. assign owners.
marc_engineer: noted. I'll push a small change to the estimator and run the regression job. if regression passes, we can roll to prod tomorrow with a short maintenance window.
lina_support: thanks team — I'll close the customer escalations after the 2h update and link this thread.
marc_engineer: thanks all. if anyone sees an unexpected OOM in canary shout out immediately.
nate_oncall: will keep watch until 03:00 UTC. :eyes:
